newsitem.title: ITALY: Low Italian CPI lays base for economy - Ciampi.
newsitem.headline: Low Italian CPI lays base for economy - Ciampi.

text.p: The sharp fall in inflation registered this month will open the way for an economic pick-up, Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said in a statement.
Earlier, preliminary data from 11 Italian cities pointed to inflation falling to 1.7 percent year-on-year in April from 2.2 percent in March.
"This is the result of a stabilty policy followed by the government," Ciampi said. "It lays the basis for a recovery in production."
The treasury minister said the fall in inflation had been brought about by the government's incomes policy, the overhaul of state accounts and a monetary policy based on stability.
"This is a guarantee for the future. There will be absolutely no fears of inflation rising, even with the expected increase in demand," he said.
The Italian economy grew just 0.7 percent in 1996. The government expects gross domestic product growth of 1.2 percent this year.
